llc.formation_notes: Expedited processing +$35 (total $85); next day +$100, same day +$200, two-hour +$400. Publication of a notice of the Articles is required (A.R.S. § 29-3201) unless the statutory agent's street address is in Maricopa or Pima County, in which case the Commission publishes it automatically on its website. Name reservation $10.

annual_report.name: None for LLCs
annual_report.due: Arizona LLCs do not file an annual report with the Corporation Commission

sources.title: Schedule of Fees, Limited Liability Companies (Rev. 3.2026)
Instructions L010i Articles of Organization
sources.quote: If your statutory agent street address is outside of Maricopa or Pima county, you will need to publish notice in a newspaper.

pte_elective_tax.rate_note: Entity-level tax election (A.R.S. § 43-1014) for partnerships and S corporations, tax years beginning 2022, at the highest individual rate (2.5%). Electing entities with taxable income over $150,000 in the prior year must make estimated payments.

sources.title: A.R.S. 43-1014 Entity-level tax election; partnerships; S corporations
sources.quote: may consent to be taxed at the entity level at a tax rate that is the same as the highest tax rate prescribed by section 43-1011

personal_exemption.notes: No personal exemption; dependent credit raised from $100 to $125 per dependent under 17 for 2026 (SB 1861/HB 4168, 2026). Standard deduction base in statute: $15,750 single / $31,500 MFJ (raised retroactively to 2025), indexed for inflation like the federal basic standard deduction; ADOR's 2026 indexed amount could not be read (azdor.gov blocks automated access). If indexed exactly like the federal deduction it would be $16,100 / $32,200 - unverified.

income_tax_2026.surtaxes: None for ordinary income (the Prop 208 surcharge was struck down). Optional small business income tax at 2.5% (A.R.S. 43-1711).

sources.title: A.R.S. 43-1011 Version 1 - Taxes and tax rates
sources.quote: the tax is 2.5% of taxable income.

sources.title: A.R.S. 43-1041 Optional standard deduction
sources.quote: In the case of a single person or a married person filing separately, the standard deduction is $15,750, subject to subsection H of this section.

sources.title: SB 1861 Senate Fact Sheet (as enacted, 2026)
sources.quote: Increases the Dependent Tax Credit from $100 to $125 for each dependent who is under 17 years old

estimated_tax.required_if: Arizona gross income exceeded $75,000 ($150,000 joint) in both the current and preceding year; no penalty if the Arizona liability due on the return is under $1,000
estimated_tax.notes: Form 140ES; dates follow the federal pattern per A.R.S. 43-581(D) (2026 booklet not readable automatically).

unemployment_2026.notes: From the DES FY2026 rate chart (UIT-0603A) as shown in search results; the PDF itself is behind bot protection and was not read directly. New employers generally keep 2.0% for at least two calendar years.

notable: No annual report for LLCs and only a $50 filing fee, but newspaper publication is required when the statutory agent is outside Maricopa and Pima counties (https://www.azcc.gov/docs/default-source/corps-files/instructions/l010i-instructions-articles-of-organization.pdf)
Estimated tax is only mandatory above $75,000 / $150,000 of Arizona gross income (https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/00581.htm)
Flat 2.5% income tax; Arizona cities levy transaction privilege (sales) tax but no local income tax (https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/01011.01.htm)
uncertain: 2026 standard deduction: statute base $15,750 / $31,500 is inflation-indexed each year; ADOR's 2026 figure not readable (azdor.gov returns a bot challenge). Left null.
SUTA 2026 figures read from search-index text of the official DES rate chart, not the PDF itself.
2026 Form 140ES due dates not read from the booklet (blocked); taken as the standard federal-pattern dates.
